component: HOME phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001): up to 3 dwelling units per lot, including tiny homes
coverage: Citywide, lots zoned SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3
coding_notes: effective_date is the date the city began accepting applications (2024-02-05); the city page gives no separate effective date. Also removes the primary/secondary distinction and the accessory-apartment and guest-house use categories (ADUs become 2- and 3-unit uses), and the limit on unrelated adults. Two- and three-unit uses: 40% building coverage, 45% impervious cover. FAR tiers by unit count not coded (the ordinance text was not read; not on the city summary page). Single-family use stays under Subchapter F (McMansion). Parking: see TX-4805000-parking-2023. Second coder (2026-10-18): applications-open date confirmed as the start date. Cap of 3 confirmed by the second coder from the city's Phase 1 summary (up to three housing units, including tiny homes, on SF-1/SF-2/SF-3; applies only to duplex, two-unit and three-unit residential uses; single-family use stays under Subchapter F). The city's note that lots created before 2025-06-16 with no more than four units need no drainage review is a later drainage rule, not a HOME unit cap. Building coverage 40% and impervious cover 45% for these uses in all districts (impervious cover up from the pre-HOME SF-1 limit); garages and carports count toward both. Building Official policy memo PM2024-0002 (2024-04-29) confirms the ordinance created a 'three-unit residential' use (three detached units, a unit plus a duplex, or one attached triplex) and, from 2024-04-29, lets triplexes be reviewed under the International Residential Code instead of the IBC when site-plan exempt, at most 3 stories and sprinklered (a cost-lowering implementation step, not coded as its own row). Ben's research workbook (2026-10-27, lotline-data/manual/texas), from Ord. 20231207-001 Part 21: in effect 2023-12-18, for applications filed on or after 2024-02-05. effective_date stays 2024-02-05, the first day the new rules could be used; the legal effective date is 2023-12-18. Checked against Austin_HOME_Phase1_Ord_20231207-001.pdf (2026-10-30): Part 4 (p. 2) Three-Unit Residential 'P' in SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3 and Part 5 maximum dwelling units per lot 3; Part 2 redefines multifamily as four or more units; Part 21 (p. 13) 'This ordinance takes effect on December 18, 2023. This ordinance applies only to an application filed on or after February 5, 2024.' FAR inside the Subchapter F area (§25-2-773(E), pp. 5-6): duplex or two-unit site 'the greater of 0.55 or 3,200 square feet', three-unit site the greater of 0.65 or 4,350 sq ft, any new unit the greater of 0.4 or 2,300 sq ft (not coded in far_cap because it is not a single FAR every lot gets).

component: Unified Development Code amendments: ADUs may have separate utilities, one-bedroom limit removed, up to two stories, smaller setbacks

coverage: Citywide
coding_notes: Council approved 191 UDC amendments (article dated 2022-11-03, vote 'Thursday' = 2022-11-03); changes take effect Jan. 1 (2023). Owner occupancy already required by city ordinance and kept. ADU size cap, ADUs per lot and by-right status not in the source: left null. Second coder (2026-10-18) supplied the UDC text: owner occupancy confirmed (the owner must live in the principal unit or the ADU and may not rent the owner-occupied unit). Size: an ADU may not exceed 800 sq ft or 50% of the primary structure's gross floor area (excluding covered porches), up to 1,600 sq ft, in single-family districts other than FR; 1,200 sq ft in RE. adu_max_sqft=800 is the size every lot gets (same convention as Columbus: the floor of the cap). Ben's research workbook (2026-10-27, lotline-data/manual/texas): Information Bulletin 402 (dated 2023-01-01) and the city ADU page agree with this row: one ADU in R-1 to R-6 and RM-4 to RM-6, owner occupancy by an affidavit recorded with Bexar County, up to 800 sq ft or 50% of the main house (at most 1,600), a parking space only above 800 sq ft. Ben's research workbook (2026-10-29, lotline-data/manual/texas): the amending ordinance is Ord. 2022-11-03-0831, adopted 2022-11-03, effective 2023-01-01 (city council-approved amendment notice of 2022-11-04 and the city's UDC adoption table: https://www.sanantonio.gov/Portals/0/Files/NHSD/Coordinated%20Housing%20Web-page/RemovingBarriers/HC.NHSD%20UDC%20Amendments%2011.4.2022.pdf; https://www.sa.gov/Directory/Departments/DSD/Constructing/Land-Development/UDC). Not checked against a local PDF (none for San Antonio).

component: SB 15 (2025): new single-family tracts of 5+ acres with no recorded plat cannot be required to have lots over 3,000 sq ft (30 ft wide, 75 ft deep); small lots (<=4,000 sq ft) get caps on setbacks, parking, open space and stories
parking: small lots: no covered or off-site parking, at most 1 space per unit
coverage: Cities over 150,000 people wholly or partly in a county over 300,000; unplatted tracts of 5 acres or more zoned single-family; excludes land near airports and military bases
coding_notes: Signed 2025-06-20 (adoption_date = signature). Covers Austin, Houston, San Antonio, Dallas, Fort Worth and other large cities, but only new subdivisions of 5+ acres: little effect on infill. Setbacks capped at 15 ft front, 10 ft back, 5 ft side; open space/permeable cap 30%; must allow 3 stories. HOA and deed restrictions still apply. parking_min_per_unit is the cap on what a city may require.

parking: one off-street space required (was two); none within 1/4 mile of an activity corridor
coverage: SF-3 and less restrictive districts, lots of at least 5,750 sq ft; not SF-1 or SF-2
coding_notes: Council vote 7-4 on 2015-11-19 (Austin Monitor, 2015-11-20). coverage: Single-family districts (R-1ac(A) to R-5(A)); a board case or an overlay rezoning is needed
coding_notes: NO ADU RULE (adus_per_lot = 0): the city ADU page says ADUs 'are not allowed to be built by right in most cases'. Routes: §51A-4.209(b)(6)(E) board special exception (non-rental, deed-restricted; or rentable with an owner-occupancy deed restriction and possible extra parking) and the §51A-4.510(c) ADU overlay (neighborhood petition, CPC and Council). Rentable terms where granted: 700 sq ft or 25% of the main house, whichever is greater; one parking space unless within 1,200 ft of a DART stop. 2 rentable ADUs granted 2018-2020. Framework adopted 2018-06-27 (Ords. 30930/30931, from the city page's file names; effective date not found, coded as the adoption date). Before 2018 only the non-rental special exception existed (adoption date not found). The 2020 by-right proposal (DCA190-007) was held by ZOAC on 2020-10-01 and suspended; no by-right ordinance found through the 2026-05-19 board minutes. Both routes need a board case or a rezoning, so adus_per_lot = 0 and by_right = False are confirmed. Corrected 2026-10-30 (#3-4 in tx-corrections-2026-10-29.csv, Ben's decision): Effective 2018-06-30: Ords. 30930 and 30931 take effect on passage and publication, published 2018-06-30 (Dallas_Ord_30930_ADU_BOA.pdf pp. 8-9; Dallas_Ord_30931_ADU_Overlay.pdf pp. 9-10). Adoption stays 2018-06-27.

component: Accessory dwelling allowed in one-family districts only when not rented or used as a separate residence (habitable accessory structure, Zoning Ordinance §5.301)

No owner-occupancy rule and no numeric size cap (accessory structures may not exceed the main house, §5.300(c)); utilities through the main house's meters (§5.300(b)). §5.301 dates from 2003/2004 and was last amended by Ord. 20454-10-2012 (adopted 2012-10-09; content of that change not described). Not checked against a local PDF (none for Fort Worth).
